name: Everyday Science: Quiz 3
grading_style:
Reasoning points need the reasoning on paper: a bare result gets only the result point.
Ignore spelling mistakes as long as the word is recognizable.

questions.prompt: How does an airplane fly? Explain why.
questions.answer_key: The wing meets the air at an angle (and is curved), so it turns the air that passes it downward. Pushing air down pushes the wing up with an equal and opposite force (Newton's third law): that force is the lift.

criteria.description: Says the wing pushes (deflects) air downward, or that the wing produces lift.
Explains that pushing air down pushes the wing up (action and reaction, Newton's third law).
hints: Re-read what you wrote, then think about what happens to the wing while it pushes the air.
Think about action and reaction: when you push something, what does it do to you?
When the wing throws air down, the air pushes the wing with an equal and opposite force. Which way does that force point, and what does it do to the plane?

criteria.description: Mentions the wing's angle (angle of attack) or shape turning the air.
hints: Look at how the wing meets the oncoming wind: is it perfectly flat against it?
Think about how the wing is set against the wind, and how that changes the air's path.
A wing is not flat to the wind: it meets the air at an angle, a bit like your hand out of a car window. What does that angle do to the air that passes under it?

transfer.prompt: How can a stunt plane fly upside down?

questions.prompt: Why do you feel cold when you get out of a swimming pool, even on a warm day?
questions.answer_key: The water left on the skin evaporates, and evaporating needs energy: the water takes that heat from your skin, so the skin cools down.

criteria.description: Says the water on the skin evaporates.
hints: Re-read your answer: what happens to the water left on your skin once you are out?
Think about where the water on your skin goes when it disappears.
The water on your skin slowly turns into vapour in the air. What is that change called, and what does it need?

criteria.description: Explains that evaporating water takes heat (energy) from the skin.
hints: Re-read what you wrote: where does the water get what it needs to turn into vapour?
Think about energy: changing from liquid to gas needs energy. Where does it come from?
Water needs energy to evaporate, and the closest source is your warm skin. What happens to your skin when something keeps taking its energy?

transfer.prompt: Why does a fan make you feel cooler when you are sweating?

questions.prompt: Why does ice float on water? Give one example of this in nature.
questions.answer_key: Ice is less dense than liquid water: water expands when it freezes. Examples: lakes freeze from the top down, icebergs float in the sea.

criteria.description: Ice is less dense than liquid water (water expands when it freezes).
hints: Re-read your answer: compare a cup of ice with a cup of water. Which one is heavier?
Think about what happens to the size of water when it freezes.
Water takes up more space when it freezes, so the same amount of ice is spread over a bigger volume. What does that do to its density?

criteria.description: Gives a sensible example from nature.
hints: Re-read your answer and think of a place outdoors where you have seen ice on water.
Think about what happens to a lake or the sea in the cold.
In winter, a frozen lake has ice on top and liquid water underneath. Where else in nature does ice float?

transfer.prompt: If ice sank instead of floating, what would happen to a lake during a long winter?
